BACKPORT: drm/edid: Add DMT modes with ID > 0x50 commit bfcd74d2aeda25a78f7cc92f80650218b1bce0ca Author: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Date: Thu Apr 2 17:02:11 2015 +0300 drm/edid: Add DMT modes with ID > 0x50 DMT Version 1.0, Rev. 13 lists a bunch of new modes we don't currently have in our dmt mode table. So add them. The order may look a bit weird since it's not sorted based on the DMT ID, but this is the order they appear in the standard. I suppose they are ordered by the resolution, pixel clock, or some such factor. I decided that it's perhaps best to keep the same order as the spec. UPSTREAM: iommu/arm-smmu: Enable bypass transaction caching for ARM SMMU 500 The ARM SMMU identity mapping performance was poor compared with the DMA mode. It was found that enable caching would restore the performance back to normal. The S2CRB_TLBEN bit in the ACR register would allow for caching of the stream to context register bypass transaction information. Reviewed-by: Robin Murphy <robin.murphy@arm.com> Signed-off-by: Feng Kan <fkan@apm.com> Signed-off-by: Will Deacon <will.deacon@arm.com> (cherry picked from commit 74f55d34414c866dbf3a69e28a2f963abe61ca58) BUG=chromium:795946 TEST=Build and boot Change-Id: I074a9d887421e93cf8f97e318e537355a8b9d56e Signed-off-by: Vivek Gautam <vivek.gautam@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/914662 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

[moblab] Hide upstart errors until moblab has booted. An upstart service 'moblab-bootup-status-init' is started alongside mobmonitor-init and is killed by upstart after all jobs have attempted to start, or after 2 minutes. I traced through the upstart dependency tree and added all moblab leaf nodes to the 'stop on' for this job. So the bootup-status-init job will only be ended if the entire moblab upstart tree starts. BUG=chromium:645676 TEST=On local moblab device. Multiple test reboots, and force the test scenario by starting the bootup status service and killing a required service. Change-Id: Ia67ce46d272bf765aa4f419f40c5eff4d3eb3e0e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/949093 Commit-Ready: Matt Mallett <mattmallett@chromium.org> Tested-by: Matt Mallett <mattmallett@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Keith Haddow <haddowk@chromium.org>

[moblab] Hide upstart errors until moblab has booted. An upstart service 'moblab-bootup-status-init' is started alongside mobmonitor-init and is killed by upstart after all jobs have attempted to start, or after 2 minutes. While this service is running, upstart service errors are demoted to warnings, and no actions will be recommended. Once the job completes, any services not running will be promoted back to errors. BUG=chromium:645676 TEST=On local moblab device. Multiple test reboots, and force the test scenario by starting the bootup status service and killing a required service. rockchip: Fix PostProcThread crash When supporting recoverable request error, we assumed metadata it the last returned result, so we force returning all buffers before that to avoid buffer leak and keep the results and request error message in sync. But that is no longer true after we made the post processing asynchronous in: 4c4b04f5 rockchip: process caputre stream in independent thread when video snapshot So the PostProcThread may crash when trying to access resources which are already freed before metadata done. Adjust request error handling to avoid that. BUG=b:72365664, b:73868843 TEST=test on my scarlet: 1/ pass CTS RobustnessTest#testMandatoryOutputCombinations 2/ fake random request error in OutputFramework's prepareRun and processFrame Change-Id: I044f58f89b6800b79cb6b2252f6caab8c25f7d1e Signed-off-by: Jeffy Chen <jeffy.chen@rock-chips.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/939122 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Hung-yu Wu <hywu@chromium.org>

FAFT: Increase the hold_pwr_button_poweroff time to 5 seconds in FAFT config This change increases the duration of holding power button to power off the device to 5 seconds. Previously hold_pwr_button_poweroff time is set to 2 seconds, and test failed to shutdown the device within 2 seconds of power button press. In Chrome EC as per common/power_button_x86.c, power button has to be pressed for 4 seconds to shutdown the device. So keeping the hold_pwr_button_poweroff time as 5 seconds to make sure device shutdown properly. BUG=None Branch=None TEST= Verified firmware_ConsecutiveBootPowerButton test for 100 iterations, test is passing. Change-Id: I93e5190376b041dc7a78446dc40c3b27efa7e718 Signed-off-by: Lenine Ajagappane <leninex.ajagappane@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/949422 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Naresh Solanki <naresh.solanki@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Wai-Hong Tam <waihong@google.com>
